data.title: FBI crime database hacked: CNN
data.description:
The FBI is investigating a potential breach of its nationwide criminal information database used by federal, state, and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks, CNN reported, citing two people briefed on the matter.

The attack on the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) by apparent hackers marks the second such incident affecting the nation’s top law enforcement agency this year.

A hack targeting an FBI jobs website exposed sensitive employee personal data in September. That attack, blamed on a group called ShinyHunters, led to the arrest of a Canadian cybersecurity researcher and author last month.

The latest hack on the FBI comes amid growing concerns over U.S. cybersecurity efforts after a series of extensive outages impacted several federal and private organizations, including the FAA and Microsoft (MSFT). 

“Every day, officers across the country rely on NCIC to identify wanted fugitives, check for outstanding warrants, and access information that can directly impact officer and public safety," said an ex-FBI official with expertise in leading investigations into cybercriminal groups.

“My concern isn’t simply whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on,” the former official added.

The FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNN.

data.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ on U.S. firms building data centers abroad
data.description:
President Donald Trump has said that his administration will ban U.S. companies from building data centers in other countries, and those who do so will face a “tremendous tax,” a policy move that caught his own staff members by surprise.

"We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," Trump said during a press conference at the White House on Friday after returning from his trip to Asia. “I don’t know if that’s a breaking story,” Trump added. “I haven’t even said that to my people. But I’m telling them now they’re here.”

His remarks came after public backlash against data centers fueled victories for some of the Democratic candidates who pledged tougher regulations on their construction in states such as Texas in the lead-up to the U.S. midterm elections.

The massive warehouse-style buildings incorporating numerous computer chips are crucial to the AI boom, as they help run popular large language models such as Claude and ChatGPT. The U.S. is home to about 3,000 data centers, while another 1,500 structures are in various stages of development as of April, according to the Pew Research Center.

“We’re going to fight very hard for the data centers,” Trump said, noting that "we're going to keep it all in this country.”

If implemented, Trump's policy will be a major headwind for AI hyperscalers such as Meta (META) and Alphabet (GOOG), which have signed agreements worth billions of dollars to build overseas data centers as part of business and regulatory requirements.

“We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they’re great places. They have energy, and they have everything. They’re tremendous assets,” Trump said.

data.title: Big banks, crypto stocks, neoclouds among losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages finished the week deep in the red as the S&P 500 entered correction territory, all while investors digested Anthropic’s landmark IPO and closely monitored Nvidia’s latest earnings report.

Large U.S. bank stock prices formed the 'death cross' bearish technical chart pattern this week, with the KBW Bank Index's (BKX) 50-day moving average falling below its 200-day moving average.

The week saw  JPMorgan Chase (JPM) face a "technical issue" that had caused customers' transactions to take longer to process on Monday. Other bank stocks, such as Bank of America (BAC), US Bank (USB), and Wells Fargo (WFC), were also impacted.

Meanwhile, bitcoin (BTC-USD) sank as Wall Street’s enthusiasm on technology and artificial intelligence fizzled out, accompanying a selloff that dipped the cryptocurrency below $58K.

Among megacap financial stocks, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial (MUFG) led the weekly losers, shedding 14.43% of its value to close the week at $18.68.

The Japanese banking giant had reported its first-half financial results last week, revising its full fiscal year earnings target higher to ¥2,800B from ¥2,700B. The stock's 14-day RSI fell to 26.32 on Friday, indicating heavy selling pressure.

"Downside risk remains elevated — I see no convincing technical or fundamental catalyst for a reversal yet," said Anton Kharitonov, expert at Traders Union.

Goldman Sachs (GS) (-13.73% W/W to $790.69) and Morgan Stanley (MS) (-13.10% W/W to $165.67) were the next major losers in the category, despite leading Anthropic's blockbuster IPO this week.

Among largecap stocks, Pershing Square (PS) led the losers, retreating 24.83% from the previous week to $33.61. Bill Ackman's hedge fund disclosed notable shifts in its portfolio this week for the quarter ended September 30.

Crypto stocks Circle Internet (CRCL) (-23.62% W/W to $47.51) and Robinhood Markets (HOOD) (-20.15% W/W to $62.17) were among notable decliners amid the crypto rout.

For midcap stocks, StoneX (SNEX) was the top loser, retreating 36.02% to $36.63. The company's fiscal Q4 earnings failed to meet Wall Street expectations. While operating revenue grew from a year ago but fell from fiscal Q3, its expenses rose both from the prior quarter and a year ago.

IREN (IREN) lost 34.95% of its value to close the week at $11.82. Neocloud stocks dropped after Nvidia reversed its post-earnings gains. Nvidia's neocloud commitments total $32B through 2032.

Strive (ASST) (-32.07% W/W to $14.51), Abacus Global (ABX) (-30.19% W/W to $6.15), and MARA Holdings (MARA) (-27.25% W/W to $5.09) were the top smallcap decliners.

data.title: SA Asks: Should Nvidia bring back Jensen Huang?
data.description:
Should Nvidia (NVDA) bring back Jensen Huang as CEO?

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Bashar Issa, Victor Dergunov, Danil Sereda, and The Techie for their thoughts.

Bashar Issa: Part of me wants Jensen Huang to stay out to break the “indispensable key person” myth used to justify billions in executive compensation, money that would otherwise go to investors who are actually taking the risk.

Moreover, as I mentioned in a recent article, Jensen Huang has been the hawk of the AI industry, pushing aggressive infrastructure buildout, adoption, and utilization by bringing all the players together. That control is one factor behind NVDA’s spectacularly high margins: for every $1 in COGS, Nvidia (NVDA) generates $4 in revenue. 

That greed and opportunism aren't what the AI sector needs right now. High GPU costs are distorting data center unit economics, making everyone nervous, and creating market volatility. The sector needs a slowdown. The next phase is low margins and higher volumes to facilitate broader adoption, and Jensen Huang isn't the one to get us there.

Victor Dergunov: Jensen Huang is too much of a liability for Nvidia (NVDA) right now given the circumstances, and I don't envision him returning as CEO. It's possible he could come back in a more limited capacity, possibly as a consultant/executive, but ultimately, he would have much less control over the company and its future.

Danil Sereda: I think bringing back Jensen Huang right now would be a strategic and governance mistake, although tactically it would help Nvidia (NVDA) regain some of its lost billions in market cap in the short term. 

As I addressed it in my recent article on Nvidia (NVDA), Huang was an irreplaceable visionary founder, no questions about it. But Nvidia (NVDA) isn't a startup anymore that can be a one-man show, so to speak. He made a few mistakes, and the board accepted his resignation with no desire to reinstate him at this time. I think that's fair. 

I also think that reinstating him would not make the intense federal scrutiny disappear. He is now expected to appear before House committees on Dec. 1 as an ex-CEO, not a current one. Given the questions that might be asked, if he returns before then, it could reignite regulatory chaos and undermine the credibility of the board.

Again, the board is probably the most important thing in a corporate structure, especially for a company with a multi-trillion-dollar market cap. Nvidia (NVDA) is likely to be fine because its operational engine didn't leave with its founder.

So, my short answer is no, Nvidia doesn't need to bring Jensen back. It can grow without him with the new, multi-role management structure in place.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

The Techie: The board was too quick to take action on Jensen Huang’s resignation. To me, it’s very clear that Jensen should be brought back into the company, if not in the capacity of CEO, then in another position. That said, I don’t think we will see that happening, and I think that sooner or later the market must stop beating a dead horse. 

The question to me now is who could replace him and how long that will take, because the company needs a clear leader to navigate everything happening, from anti-China laws to the custom ASIC threat.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: 11 of 14 reporting firms beat EPS estimates; 12 grow Y/Y profits
data.description:
Earnings season continues with 14 companies reporting quarterly results across communication services, consumer discretionary, consumer staples, and information technology.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Out of the 14 companies reporting, 11 exceeded EPS expectations, while 3 came in-line. Notably, 12 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth.

Top Line: Out of the 14 companies reporting, 12 exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, all 14 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

The Walt Disney Company (DIS): shares fell 1.48% post-earnings after beating Q4 estimates, with adjusted EPS of $1.77 (vs. $1.68 consensus) and revenue rising 16% Y/Y to $25.95B (vs. $25.2B est.). For FY27, Disney guided for double-digit adjusted EPS growth and ~8% segment operating income growth (ex-53rd week), while raising its annual dividend by 33% to $2.00/share.

The Home Depot (HD): shares fell 2.45% post-earnings after beating Q3 estimates, with adjusted EPS of $3.86 (vs. $3.84 consensus) and revenue rising 4.9% Y/Y to $43.4B on 2.2% comparable sales growth. Management projected ~4.5% FY26 sales growth and 2.0% EPS growth, while naming CFO Richard McPhail to succeed Ted Decker as CEO effective November 23.

Lowe's Companies (LOW): shares rose 1.05% post-earnings after beating Q3 estimates, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.10 (vs. $2.90 consensus) and comparable sales rising 1.8% (vs. +0.4% est.) on a 17.4% jump in online sales. Management guided full-year sales to ~$92.5B (vs. $92.1B consensus) and adjusted EPS to $12.25 (vs. $12.27 est.), with comparable sales seen flat to +0.5%.

The TJX Companies (TJX): jumped 8.05% post-earnings after Q3 revenue rose 5.5% Y/Y to $15.95B on 4% comparable sales growth (beating the +3.8% consensus), while non-GAAP EPS of $1.34 matched estimates. Management guided full-year comp sales growth to 4% and EPS to $5.17–$5.20 (vs. $5.23 consensus), alongside plans to buy back ~$3.0B in stock during FY27.

Target Corporation (TGT): shares rose 4.01% post-earnings after a Q3 beat-and-raise, as tariff-refund tailwinds ($0.50/share) and <1% average ticket growth overshadowed 5.6% comparable sales growth (vs. 3.61% estimates) and adjusted EPS of $2.65 (vs. $2.08 estimates). Management raised FY26 guidance to ~6% sales growth ($111B) and adjusted EPS of $10.65–$11.40, while lifting capex to $5B–$6B.

Tyson Foods (TSN): jumped 8.72% post-earnings despite a 47% Y/Y drop in FQ4 adjusted EPS to $0.61 (vs. $0.62 consensus) as reported revenue rose 5.2% to $14.59B (-4.0% comparable). Deeper beef losses ($171M) and tighter chicken margins (8.7% vs. 12.7%) weighed on profits, while management projected FY27 sales to decline 3.5%–5.5% with $1.7B–$2.15B in adjusted operating income.

Walmart (WMT): slipped 1.04% post-earnings despite beating Q3 estimates, as a cautious holiday outlook tempered results. Adjusted EPS of $0.65 topped the $0.64 consensus, while U.S. comparable sales rose 2.9% (vs. 2.8% estimates) on a 23% jump in U.S. e-commerce; management guided FY27 revenue growth to 4.9%–5.2% and EPS to $2.84–$2.89 (midpoint $2.865 vs. $2.89 estimates).

Palo Alto Networks (PANW): surged 6.42% post-earnings after an FQ1 FY27 beat-and-raise, with adjusted EPS of $1.05 (vs. $0.97 consensus) and revenue rising 39% Y/Y to $3.45B (vs. $3.31B est.). Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to $14.52B–$14.57B and adjusted EPS to $4.26–$4.30 (vs. $4.18 estimates), alongside announcing a $4.5B all-stock deal to acquire Applied Compute.

NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA): shares fell 2.89% post-earnings after delivering a strong Q3 beat-and-raise, reporting adjusted EPS of $2.68 (beating consensus by $0.21) and revenue surging 103.2% Y/Y to $115.84B ($7.13B above forecasts). Management guided Q4 revenue to ~$130B (±3%, vs. $124.89B estimates) and lifted FY28 revenue growth expectations to ~75% Y/Y, while noting it could exhaust its remaining $227.3B share buyback authorization by FY28.

Intuit (INTU): plunged ~12.8% post-earnings as soft guidance overshadowed a Q1 FY27 beat, with revenue up 12% Y/Y to $4.4B and non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 topping the $2.64 consensus. Amid Credit Karma softness, management guided Q2 revenue to $4.93B–$4.95B (vs. $5.11B estimates) and non-GAAP EPS to $3.17–$3.22 (vs. $3.94 estimates), while affirming FY27 non-GAAP EPS of $22.88–$23.12 (vs. $23.81 estimates). Intuit also agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons, acquired AI platform Sequence, and declared a $1.38/share quarterly dividend.

Keysight Technologies (KEYS): shares fell 7.1% post-earnings after a Q4 beat-and-raise, with adjusted EPS of $3.61 (vs. $3.37 consensus) and revenue jumping 41% Y/Y to $1.99B (vs. $1.95B estimates). For Q1 FY27, management guided adjusted EPS to $3.63–$3.69 (vs. $3.21 estimates) and revenue to $2.04B–$2.06B (vs. $1.96B estimates).

Earnings next week:

As earnings season rolls on, investors are tracking key reports across consumer discretionary, consumer staples, health care, industrials, and information technology.

data.title: Broadcom AI outlook in focus beyond quarterly results, Goldman says
data.description:
For Broadcom (AVGO), the focus would likely be beyond its quarterly results and on whether demand for AI chips can remain strong through 2028, as per Goldman Sachs analysts."We expect modest upside to guidance, but believe the stock will ultimately be driven more by clarity on the sustainability of AI spending into 2028, and Broadcom’s competitive position at key accounts such as Google," analysts at Goldman Sachs said. 

AVGO stock was down 10% on Friday trading after a report revealed Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) is cutting planned shipments of its Broadcom-designed AI chips for 2027, while increasing orders for chips designed by MediaTek. 

Concerns are growing about shortages of land, electricity, and buildings needed to house large-scale data centers. There are also questions about whether smaller cloud providers focused on AI will be able to secure enough outside funding to support their expansion. These emerging cloud providers account for about 6.3 gigawatts of Broadcom's planned 10 gigawatts of custom AI chip deployments in 2027. In 2028 emerging cloud providers are expected to account for about 75% of Broadcom's planned custom AI chip deployments. 

Broadcom's competitive position is also at focus, especially after stock lost more than 10% value on Friday following reports of Google cutting Broadcom-designed AI chips while increasing orders for chips designed by MediaTek.  

"We believe incremental detail on the durability of key customer engagements for next-generation XPUs as competitive intensity increases from providers such as MediaTek, could be impactful for the stock," Goldman analysts said. 

Goldman cut the price target on Broadcom to $460 from $540, as it reduced the valuation multiple it applies to the company's expected earnings, from 30 times to 25 times.

Broadcom will report its fourth quarter results on December 9.

data.title: Bitcoin drops to lowest level in more than two years
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) fell to its lowest level in more than two years late Friday as a widespread selloff in artificial intelligence stocks amid concerns over another Fed rate hike weighed on the ​world's largest cryptocurrency by market value.

The original cryptocurrency lost 5.1% to reach $55,830 ​by 11:13 p.m. ET on Friday, recording its lowest level since September 2024 and extending its five-day decline to roughly 15%.

Bitcoin’s (BTC-USD) selloff has coincided with a broader decline in the tech sector as investors review their investments in riskier assets amid fears over another Federal Reserve rate hike next month.

The abrupt resignation of Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s (ANT) record-breaking IPO, and increasing regulatory risks for the cryptocurrency industry following the Democrats’ ​victory ⁠in the midterm elections have added another dimension to the bitcoin’s valuation debate.

“One explanation circulating in the market was that investors had been selling Bitcoin to free up capital for Anthropic's IPO,” wrote Seeking Alpha analyst BloFin Research.  “However, Bitcoin has yet to see a meaningful rebound since the IPO, although one trading session is too early to determine whether such capital rotation will eventually occur,” the analyst added.

data.title: Capricor reviewing operations as FDA rejects cell therapy
data.description:
Capricor Therapeutics (CAPR) announced that its operating expenses are under review after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Friday declined to approve its cell therapy candidate Deramiocel for the second time in less than two years.

In a statement, the company said the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter in connection with its resubmitted Biologics License Application for Deramiocel, rejecting the one-time therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a rare neuromuscular disorder.

The FDA attributed the decision to concerns over Deramiocel's effectiveness, among other issues. “The CRL states that the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies,” Capricor (CAPR) added.

The company sought U.S. approval for its lead asset after the FDA issued a complete response letter for its original BLA in July 2025. However, an independent advisory panel of the agency refused to recommend it for approval, noting that the drug lacked efficacy against cardiomyopathy in Duchenne.

Capricor (CAPR) shares plunged over 78% in post-market trading on Friday after the announcement.

The company reported $198.5M in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of Sept. 30, which it said would be adequate to fund its operations over the next 12 months. However, given the setback, the San Diego, California-based biotech is reviewing its operating expenses to extend the cash runway.

data.title: From ChatGPT to Claude deals: Walmart looks like an agentic AI winner
data.description:
Walmart (WMT) developed its generative AI shopping assistant Sparky to very little fanfare as part of a broader push into what it called adaptive retail. While early buzz was light, the payoff for Walmart (WMT) investing in Sparky is just beginning.

CEO John Furner noted that in Walmart's third quarter, U.S. usage of Sparky climbed 129% year over year, with baskets associated with the assistant running 40% larger. The AI assistant helps shoppers discover items, plan meals, summarize reviews, turn photos of handwritten lists into carts, and reorder staples based on inventory positioning, pricing, and delivery speed. 

Walmart (WMT) began its efforts to scale generative AI across customers, members, associates, and partners in 2024. The retail giant introduced Sparky in June 2025 inside its app and web experience, pairing text chat with voice and image inputs. Rather than relying on a single bot for everything, Walmart (WMT) structured its AI ecosystem around specialized agents, separating shopping discovery in Sparky from dedicated customer-support automation that handles order lookup, returns, and delivery updates. The company also expanded beyond proprietary surfaces by partnering earlier this year with OpenAI (OPENAI) to bring Sparky into ChatGPT and building a Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) Gemini shopping experience.

Meanwhile, Anthropic (ANT) partnered with Walmart (WMT) to help power Sparky itself using Claude models such as Claude Sonnet 4.6. On the consumer side, rather than embedding a standalone Sparky widget inside Claude, Walmart opened its Agent Gateway, built on Anthropic's (ANT) Model Context Protocol, in October. This allows approved third-party assistants, including Claude, to search Walmart's (WMT) catalog and prepare orders directly on a shopper's behalf using user-controlled Agent Profiles and spending limits.

Looking ahead, Walmart plans to scale Sparky across more markets, languages, and shopping modes while building infrastructure for third-party AI agents. It has already rolled Sparky out in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and Sam's Club with support for languages such as Spanish and French. Next, Walmart (WMT) is introducing Agent Profiles so shoppers can set permissions, spending limits, track agent purchases separately, or revoke access, alongside a Walmart Agent Gateway to govern how approved external agents interact with its catalog.

data.title: Oil prices wrap up third straight weekly decline on strong Middle East supply outlook
data.description:
Crude oil futures edged higher on Friday but fell for the third consecutive week as recovering supply out of the Middle East outweighed concerns about ongoing strikes across the region, while President Trump continued to hold off on renewed large-scale attacks against Iran.

A stronger U.S. dollar and broader weakness across commodity markets also added to pressure on oil prices this week.

"Resilient flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain the story for energy markets broadly, extending to LNG recently," Macquarie energy strategist Walt Chancellor said in a note. "Should strength in Middle East flows and accompanying inventory builds persist, further oil price weakness would not surprise us."

Persistence of the status quo with the Iran blockade and convoys through the strait could keep pressure on oil markets, but "we cannot altogether dismiss the potential for escalation," Chancellor added.

In its World Energy Outlook, the Paris-based International Energy Agency said the global oil market is expected to return to a surplus as Middle Eastern production recovered faster than demand, forecasting an oversupply of 1.7M bbl/day in Q4 and widening to 3.8M bbl/day next year.

Data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration also pointed to improving regional supply, as Q3 oil shipments through major Middle Eastern chokepoints jumped 19% Q/Q while regional crude production reached 23.1M bbl/day in October, its highest level since the start of the Iran war, as producers expanded shipments through alternative routes.

However, Iran-backed Houthi militants said people near Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports should evacuate and urged shipping companies to remove vessels, saying they would target Saudi ports in Jeddah and the Red Sea if a Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's ‌Hodeidah port.

The warning came a day after the Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh, damaging several floors of a tower in the financial district.

Two oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said Thursday.

Iran's intensifying attacks on tankers transiting the strait, "running at roughly one incident per day in November," still add a meaningful geopolitical risk premium to the market, UOB Group analysts said in a note.

"Supply disruptions remain a risk, but near-term demand concerns tied to the AI trade unwind and broader risk-off sentiment are weighing on prices," Saxo Bank analysts wrote.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for December delivery added 0.9% to $83.98/bbl, and front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for January delivery edged up 0.6% to $92.57/bbl; for the full week, Nymex and Brent fell 5.2% and 3.4%, respectively.

U.S. natural gas (NG1:COM) futures recovered from the previous day’s losses to settle at the highest level since February 6, with the front-month December contract climbing 4.4% to $3.411/MMBtu; for the week, natgas gained 5.6%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), sank 6.8% this week.
